$comment: Gate 2.4-F evidence. The shipped continuous-protection offer is built for every guard host in ASK_AFTER_SUCCESS — the state where a one-time setup just succeeded and CallLint asks for something persistent. Both the offer OBJECT and the RENDERED TEXT are measured together: an object that discloses a component the renderer then omits would satisfy either half alone while still deceiving the person deciding. Disclosure is strict — every component's label, its artifact path and its uninstall command must appear verbatim in what the human sees, alongside the disable command and a visible [Not now]. Regenerate with `pnpm eval:phase-2.4:gates:write`.

observations.renderedText:
Protect future agent-tool changes

  CallLint can:
    • re-decide the approved agent-tool authority surface when a session starts
    • detect authority drift against the approved baseline
    • re-check upgrades of already-approved tools
    • refuse a tampered install plan (approval is bound to the exact plan digest)

  This installs persistent components (a separate decision from the install above):
    git pre-commit hook (calllint-guard:git)
      creates:   .git/hooks/pre-commit
      remove:    rm .git/hooks/pre-commit
      enable:    calllint guard install --host git

  disable later: calllint guard disable
  disclosure: sha256:7b9592e96c45ad24add0054a83f177b9442f31388dd91ba7860965a2ec3638c4
  [Enable continuous protection]   [Not now]

  Nothing persistent was installed by the step above, and nothing is
  installed by this offer. Run the enable command yourself to opt in.
